title: Understanding the physical nature of small Solar System bodies
text:
Research
My work currently spans three closely connected areas of planetary science.


Martian moons
I study the surface properties and composition of Phobos and Deimos, with particular interest in how remote-sensing observations can constrain their origin and evolution.
My work includes the analysis of visible and infrared spectroscopy and the development of methods relevant to the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission.


Asteroid thermophysics
I investigate how asteroids absorb, conduct, and emit heat, using thermal inertia, rotation, thermophysical modelling, and thermal-infrared observations to better understand the physical properties of their surfaces.
This work will be relevant for the planned Near-Earth Object Mission in the Infrared (NEOMIR), which is a part of ESA’s Planetary Defence objective.


Small-body populations
I use large astronomical datasets to investigate asteroid populations and the relationships between their physical and compositional properties.
A major part of this work involves MP3C, combining measurements of rotation, taxonomy, albedo, thermal properties, and orbital parameters.

title: Understanding the physical nature of small Solar System bodies
text:
Current work
My PhD focuses on developing and applying thermophysical models for small Solar System bodies, particularly in preparation for future observations of the Martian moons.
Alongside this, I am working on the interpretation of Phobos spectroscopy, asteroid thermal inertia, and population-scale studies using MP3C.

title: Understanding the physical nature of small Solar System bodies
text:
Selected work

Phobos and primitive asteroids
I have worked on comparing the visible-to-infrared properties of different terrains on Phobos with primitive asteroid populations, helping to place the Martian moon in the broader context of small-body composition.
View publications →


Asteroid rotation and composition
I have investigated differences in the rotational behaviour of C- and S-complex asteroids, including how their spin-rate distributions may reflect differences in internal structure and material properties.
Read more about my research →


MP3C
I contribute to the development and scientific use of the Minor Planet Physical Properties Catalogue (MP3C), which brings together a wide range of physical and compositional measurements for asteroids.
Visit MP3C →

title: Publications
section: Infrared-to-visible albedo ratio of Phobos. Comparison with primitive asteroids.
text:
Infrared-to-visible albedo ratio of Phobos. Comparison with primitive asteroids.
Thomas J. Dyer, et al.

Abstract
We compare the infrared-to-visible albedo ratio of different terrains on Phobos with primitive asteroid populations in order to investigate possible compositional similarities and differences.

section: The dependence of asteroid rotation on composition: A spectral class database for MP3C
text:
The dependence of asteroid rotation on composition: A spectral class database for MP3C
T. J. Dyer, W.-H. Zhou, C. Avdellidou, M. Delbo, D. Athanasopoulos, J. Ďurech and P. Pravec

Abstract
We investigated whether the valley that separates fast and slow rotators in rotational period–diameter space depends on asteroid composition. We approximated the composition using the asteroids’ spectral class.
